---
title: Lists and segmentation
---

Lists are how Listmonk decides who gets what. A campaign targets one or more lists; a subscriber belongs to any number of them. Most apps have a handful (the newsletter, the product announcements, the beta testers) and manage membership from code as people sign up, upgrade, and leave.

## Reading lists

```python
for lst in listmonk.lists():
    print(lst.id, lst.name, lst.type, lst.optin, lst.subscriber_count)

newsletter = listmonk.list_by_id(7)
```

[`lists()`](../reference/lists.qmd) returns every list on the instance in one request. [`list_by_id()`](../reference/list_by_id.qmd) returns a [`MailingList`](../reference/models.MailingList.qmd) and, unlike the subscriber lookups, raises rather than returning `None` when the ID is unknown. Each model carries the list's `uuid`, which you will need for opt-in confirmation below, and a `subscriber_statuses` breakdown with the count still awaiting confirmation.

## Creating and changing lists

```python
beta = listmonk.create_list('Beta testers', list_type='private', optin='single', tags=['product'])

listmonk.update_list(beta.id, description='People trying the new editor')
listmonk.update_list(beta.id, status='archived')

listmonk.delete_list(beta.id)
```

[`create_list()`](../reference/create_list.qmd) needs a name; `list_type` is `public` or `private` (public lists appear on Listmonk's public subscription form) and `optin` is `single` or `double`. Both are validated before the request goes out. [`update_list()`](../reference/update_list.qmd) sends only the fields you pass, so an update that mentions just `description` leaves everything else alone; `status` can move a list between `active` and `archived`. [`delete_list()`](../reference/delete_list.qmd) checks that the list exists first and raises if it does not.

## Membership

There are three ways to put people on lists, suited to three different moments.

At signup, pass `list_ids` to [`create_subscriber()`](../reference/create_subscriber.qmd).

For one person later on, use [`update_subscriber()`](../reference/update_subscriber.qmd) with `add_to_lists` and `remove_from_lists`. The result is the person's current lists, minus the removals, plus the additions.

For many people at once, use [`add_subscribers_to_lists()`](../reference/add_subscribers_to_lists.qmd):

```python
ok = listmonk.add_subscribers_to_lists([201, 202, 203], [7, 9])
ok = listmonk.add_subscribers_to_lists([201], [7], status='unconfirmed')
```

It de-duplicates both ID sets, marks the new subscriptions `confirmed` unless you say `unconfirmed`, and returns `False` rather than raising when either set is empty or the server answers with an error. It takes subscriber IDs, not emails, so look people up first; the [sync recipe](recipes.qmd#sync-your-user-table-into-a-list) does that in bulk.

## Single and double opt-in

A single opt-in list accepts a subscription as confirmed the moment it is made. A double opt-in list adds the person as `unconfirmed` and emails them a confirmation link; they receive campaigns only after clicking it.

When your own app has already collected consent (a checkbox on your signup form, say) you can skip the email by passing `pre_confirm=True` to `create_subscriber()`, and `update_subscriber()` always confirms the memberships it sets. When you want Listmonk to run the confirmation flow, leave `pre_confirm` off.

If you run your own confirmation page and want to confirm a double opt-in from code, use [`confirm_optin()`](../reference/confirm_optin.qmd) with the subscriber's and the list's UUIDs:

```python
sub = listmonk.subscriber_by_email('jane@example.com')
newsletter = listmonk.list_by_id(7)
confirmed = listmonk.confirm_optin(sub.uuid, newsletter.uuid)  # True or False
```

This submits Listmonk's public opt-in form rather than calling a JSON endpoint, so it reports failure as `False` instead of raising. Only call it when the person has genuinely opted in.

## Choosing a list to segment on

Lists are the right tool when membership is a decision someone made or a stage they are in: subscribed to the newsletter, enrolled in a course, invited to the beta. For slicing by a property of the person (city, plan, signup date) you do not need a list at all; store the property in `attribs` and filter with `subscribers(query_text=...)`, as shown in [Subscribers](subscribers.qmd#finding-many). Campaigns can target a list, and Listmonk's own UI can save a query as a segment, so both approaches end up usable from the campaign side.
